title: Chapter 150: The Second Lucky Draw
html:
The middle-aged man was at a loss. He had run this stall for half his life and never encountered such a request. “If that’s all you want, leave. I don’t sell the kind of cleaver you’re after.”

“Then could you sell me the one you normally use?” Chen Ge refused to give up. Useful or not, he intended to acquire a cleaver before the livestream.

“How am I supposed to run this stall without my cleaver?” The man had barely finished when a dyed-haired youth pushed through the crowd. He looked about nineteen and wore his jacket tied around his waist, yawning as he approached. The middle-aged man slammed his cleaver into the cutting board, wiped his hands on his apron, and strode over. “So you still remember where home is? Where were you last night?”

“Karaoke with friends, then the internet café.” The youth put in his earphones, plainly trying to shut the man out.

“Then why didn’t you answer your phone?” Years of butchering had made the middle-aged man far more muscular than his son. He yanked out the earphones. “I’m talking to you!”

The young man covered his ears with both hands and stood in sullen silence.

“Have you gone mute? I asked why you didn’t come home last night! You wouldn’t even answer your phone—what were you thinking?” His voice rose until customers began trying to calm him. The youth glared at his father, snatched back the earphones at the first opening, and bolted from the market.

“Come back here!” Unable to abandon his stall and give chase, the man seized his cleaver and split a bone in one furious stroke. Reading the mood, Chen Ge quietly reclaimed his money and left with the rooster.

Outside the market, he was searching for his bicycle when the youth approached him. “I heard you’re looking for a cleaver.”

“Yes, but not a new one. I need a blade that has been used for years.”

“I have one at home. Follow me, but don’t let my father see us.” The youth led him to a building near the market, told him to wait outside, and soon returned with an object wrapped in red cloth.

“My grandfather was a butcher. He planned to take this knife to his grave because he never wanted his children to follow in his trade. My stubborn father insisted on keeping it, and bad luck has followed us ever since. He lost his business, my mother died, and eventually he had to sell pork in the market just to survive.” The youth handed the bundle to Chen Ge. “The cleaver is cursed, so I won’t ask much. One hundred, and it’s yours.”

Intrigued, Chen Ge drew back the red cloth and examined the blade. His Yin Yang Vision reacted at once, his eyes stinging as though pierced by needles. Several seconds passed before the pain subsided.

The cloth concealed a single-edged blade forty centimeters long. Perhaps because it had tasted so much fresh blood, the metal had turned dark red. Grooves ran along its length, while faint crimson lines threaded through the wooden handle like veins.

Chen Ge tested its weight and found it heavier than expected. “This really is an unusual cleaver.”

The edge had long since dulled, but the oppressive air surrounding it had not faded.

“When I was little, I watched my grandfather enter the pigsty with this cleaver. Not one pig dared make a sound.” The youth glanced at the red cloth and held out his hand. “If you’re satisfied, pay me.”

“Not bad. This is exactly what I need.” Chen Ge paid him one hundred yuan and left his phone number. “If your father asks about the cleaver, tell him to call me.”

“What does this have to do with him?” the youth asked flatly before retreating inside with the money.

“Your father may be sharp-tongued and short-tempered, but life isn’t easy for him either. As far as I know, there are no slaughterhouses near Jiujiang. To keep his stock fresh, he must wake at three every morning and travel outside the city for supplies, or he’ll miss the market opening.”

…

Carrying the rooster and cleaver, Chen Ge returned to New Century Park. He still had time to spare, so he reviewed the list he had written the night before.

A live rooster, a cleaver, and salt… I have all of those. The Three-Star Trial Mission will be dangerous, though, and none of this matters if I don’t return alive.Determined to bring every advantage available, he took out the black phone, scrolled to the bottom, and fixed his gaze on the Wheel of Misfortune.

That particular feature had left him genuinely scarred. Completing the expansion mission earned me one draw, and the Haunted House has collected enough screams for me to redeem another. Surely I can’t be unlucky enough to draw a Baleful Specter twice.

Chen Ge normally avoided games governed entirely by chance. Without the pressure of a Three-Star Trial Mission, he would probably have continued ignoring the wheel.

With two chances, I might actually win something that can save my life.He tapped the screen, and the wheel began to spin. Chen Ge clasped his hands as it turned. Please, anything but another Baleful Specter.

“Ding!” The pointer came to rest. “Congratulations! You have won a unique item—White Valentine’s Candy (Seven percent chance of appearing once Zhang Ya’s affection reaches ‘Crazy About You’).

“Sincerity, purity, clarity, romance. Accepting this gift will advance your relationship to the next level.

“White Valentine’s Candy: Sweetness dances across your tongue. Once you finish the candy, Zhang Ya will appear.

“You have received the gift Zhang Ya was unable to give while alive. Zhang Ya’s affection for you has increased slightly.”

An ominous feeling settled over Chen Ge as he sat on the steps. The gift Zhang Ya couldn’t give while she was alive? Why does that sound so disturbing?

A draft brushed his neck. Turning, he discovered a bag of candy behind him, its design matching the one he had found in the dance studio at Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy. Inside lay a single white candy molded into the face of a weeping girl.

That looks like one of Zhang Ya’s roommates. Don’t tell me she turned her roommate into candy!

He returned the candy to its package and reconsidered his situation. I didn’t draw a Baleful Specter, but the prize is still tied to one. Does being near the Haunted House attract this sort of thing?

He rose and dusted himself off, washed his face, settled the rooster inside the building, and left New Century Park by bicycle.

According to the black phone, the wheel offers many different rewards. Statistically, I’m due for something useful.Facing the rising sun, he tapped the screen. The wheel spun furiously and stopped several seconds later.

What did I get?Sunlight washed over him, gilding his figure.

“Congratulations! You have won a rare item—The Crying Tape (Three percent chance of winning).

“The first time he played the tape, he knew something was wrong. Though supposedly blank, it contained white noise that could not be erased. After trying every possible method to remove it, he heard the sound he had made just before his death.

“Congratulations, Specter’s Favored! You have won another Rare Baleful Specter.

“Note: After obtaining five Baleful Specters, the title Specter’s Favored will be upgraded!”

…

Chen Ge sat beside the road with a cigarette dangling from his lips. Gazing back at New Century Park three kilometers away, he sighed. “I shouldn’t have wasted the effort coming this far.”
